open_points.subject: Cabinet Kernel publication authority
open_points.text: “A service publishes and withdraws none: its token has no such right” contradicts “the agent publishes and withdraws pointers through Cabinet Kernel” and the primary actions naming Cabinet Kernel as caller.
open_points.question: Does Cabinet Kernel’s service token authorize publish and withdraw when carrying agent authority, or are those operations invoked through some non-service authority?
options: Kernel’s token may publish and withdraw only with agent authority and a registered session
No service token, including Kernel’s, may invoke these operations
Kernel uses a separate credential or channel for agent-authority calls
open_points.default_guess: Kernel’s service token may invoke them only as agent authority, with the session and project grant checked.

open_points.subject: Owner publish replay
open_points.text: “As a write of the agent, a publish carries a request id” defines retry behavior only for the agent, although “the owner does [publish] in the owner interface.”
open_points.question: What happens when the owner retries the same publish after losing its response or submitting the form twice?
options: Owner publishes also carry a request id and return the original pointer
Each accepted owner submission creates a new version
The owner interface prevents retries by another stated mechanism
open_points.default_guess: Give owner publishes a request id and return the original pointer on retry.

open_points.subject: Publish request-id scope
open_points.text: “a retried publish — the same request id — is not a second publish” does not say within what scope request ids are unique.
open_points.question: Is sameness of a publish request id evaluated globally, per principal, per agent session, per project, per artifact type, or by some other key?
options: Globally unique
Unique per publishing principal or session
Unique per project and artifact type
Unique by a specified composite key
open_points.default_guess: Treat it as unique per authenticated principal or agent session plus operation name.

open_points.subject: Request-id reuse with different publish input
open_points.text: “the same request id … returns the pointer it made” is silent when that request id is presented again with a different project, type, `uri`, `payload_ref`, digest, or other publish input.
open_points.question: Must a reused request id with different publish content return the original pointer, be refused as an idempotency conflict, or be treated as a new publish?
options: Refuse it as an idempotency conflict
Return the original pointer regardless of changed input
Treat it as a new publish
open_points.default_guess: Refuse it as an idempotency conflict and make no change.

open_points.subject: Failed publish and request-id reuse
open_points.text: “returns the pointer it made” does not define whether a refused publish consumes or records its request id when no pointer was made.
open_points.question: May the same request id be retried after the original publish was refused, and if so is it re-evaluated against the current state?
options: Refusals do not consume the id; a retry is evaluated normally
Refusals are replayed permanently for that id
Only specified classes of refusal consume the id
open_points.default_guess: Refusals do not consume the request id; a later attempt is evaluated normally.

open_points.subject: Evidence for an artifact link
open_points.text: “Registry cannot check that the document exists, and the Kernel flow that made it is the evidence” does not name what evidence exists, where it is stored, what Registry receives or checks, or what failure occurs when publication was not produced by the required flow.
open_points.question: Is an accepted pointer merely the publisher’s unverified assertion, or must Kernel provide or retain identifiable evidence that a producer operation returned that document reference?
options: The authenticated publish is an unverified assertion; no additional evidence is required
Kernel must retain flow/run evidence outside Registry
Registry must receive and validate an evidence reference
open_points.default_guess: Treat the authenticated publish as the assertion and remove any promise that Registry relies on separately verifiable flow evidence.

open_points.subject: Evidence for owner-published links
open_points.text: The text allows “the owner [to publish] in the owner interface” but says “the Kernel flow that made it is the evidence,” although an owner publication has no Kernel flow.
open_points.question: What is the evidence or trust basis for a pointer published directly by the owner?
options: The authenticated owner action itself is sufficient evidence
The owner must supply a reference produced by a Kernel flow
Owner publication requires a separately recorded provenance value
open_points.default_guess: The authenticated, audited owner action itself is sufficient evidence.
